values: Is there a uniform bound on the Godbillon-Vey invariants of the taut foliations of a hyperbolic manifold in terms of its volume?

Unbounded Godbillon-Vey numbers on a fixed hyperbolic manifold (PR184, AMR-102-0044). Verified negative answer to literal Calegari math/0209081v1 Q10.6: one fixed closed hyperbolic M, smooth cooriented taut F_N with GV=Na and common embedded all-leaf positive circle. Credited classical-consequence research note; historical priority unresolved after bounded audit with unread-source/version gaps. No firstness, guaranteed novelty or minimal-foliation claim. Extensive AI; unrefereed, no conventional human peer review.

records.title: Unbounded Godbillon-Vey numbers on a fixed hyperbolic manifold
records.description:
Classical compact-support suspension theory gives a foliated surface-times-interval block with product endpoint collars and nonzero ordinary Godbillon-Vey integral. Placing finite stacks in one fixed pseudo-Anosov mapping torus yields smooth cooriented taut foliations with GV=Na, a>0, and the same embedded positive closed transversal meeting every leaf. This gives a negative answer to the literal unrestricted volume-bound Question 10.6 in Calegari's arXiv:math/0209081v1 (2002). Compact leaves are permitted; no minimal-foliation variant is claimed.

This is a credited consequence of classical Mather-Thurston/Tsuboi suspension theory, interval-bundle replacement documented by Gabai, and Thurston hyperbolization. A bounded primary-source audit did not authenticate an earlier explicit full consequence, but historical firstness, guaranteed novelty and present-day open status are not established. Relevant full texts remain unread, and the final 2003 target chapter was not compared. Version and access limits are documented in the supplement.

The deposit includes the research note, standalone LaTeX source, repaired exact-rational and symbolic local controls with actual ordinary/optimized reproduction, independent mathematical audits, and bounded priority ledgers. Finite controls do not replace the global existence proof. AI tools were used extensively in development, drafting, source checking, reproduction and adversarial review. This preprint is unrefereed and has not undergone conventional human peer review.
